questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The diagram shows the marginal utility (MU) an individual derives from consuming different quantities of good X. utility (utils) MU 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 quantity of good X (units) At the margin, the individual derives two units of utility from every $1 that he spends. Which quantity of good X will he purchase if the price of X is $2?
Why will the quantity demanded increase when the price of a normal good falls?

options.A: The income and substitution effects are both positive.
options.B: The income and substitution effects are both negative.
options.C: The negative income effect is greater than the positive substitution effect.
options.D: The positive income effect is greater than the negative substitution effect.

questions.questionText: A firm in a perfectly competitive industry employs two factors of production, X and Y. The table shows the factor price and the current marginal physical product of these two factors. factor X factor Y factor price $2.50 $6.00 marginal physical product 2 8 If the firm sells its product for $1 and aims to maximise profits, what should it do?

options.A: employ less of both X and Y
options.B: employ less of X and more of Y
options.C: employ more of both X and Y
options.D: employ more of X and less of Y

questions.questionText: In which situation is it likely that the demand for labour would be inelastic?

options.A: Labour and capital are close substitutes.
options.B: Labour costs are only a small proportion of total costs.
options.C: Demand for the final product that the labour produces is elastic.
options.D: A large quantity of unemployed labour is available in the economy.

questions.questionText: An actor is paid $100000 a year. The next best paid job he could get would be as a lecturer. He estimates that he currently earns an economic rent of $40000. What wage could he earn as a lecturer and what are his transfer earnings? wage as transfer a lecturer earnings ($) ($)

The schedule shows the short-run marginal cost of producing good X. units of X 1 2 3 4 5 6 marginal cost ($) 45 40 30 20 20 50 Given that the total fixed cost is $50, what level of output minimises average total cost?

options.A: 2 units B 3 units C 4 units D 5 units

questions.questionText: The table shows the quantity of inputs needed to produce different levels of output. output inputs 100 5 200 10 300 15 400 19 500 25 Over which output range do increasing returns to scale occur?
In many developed economies, large and small firms often exist side by side in the same industry. What is most likely to explain the survival of these small firms?

options.A: They each offer a much wider range of products.
options.B: They have a higher minimum efficient scale.
options.C: They pay much higher wages to their staff.
options.D: They provide a more personal level of consumer service.

questions.questionText: A bad harvest for an agricultural crop results in an increase in the total revenue received collectively by farmers. If the demand schedule remains the same, what can be concluded from this?
What is the necessary characteristic of an oligopolistic industry?

options.C: price leadership by a dominant firm

questions.questionText: The table shows a firm’s average variable cost of producing different levels of output. There are no fixed costs. units of output 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 average variable cost ($) 22 18 15 13 14 16 18 If the market price were $18, within what range of output would a profit-maximising firm in a perfectly competitive industry produce in the short-run?

options.A: 1–2 units B 3–4 units C 4–5 units D 6–7 units

questions.questionText: The diagram illustrates the working of a negative income tax system (NIT), where households with incomes above Y pay tax and those with incomes below Y receive a tax credit. t t + NIT tax 1 NIT paid Y household income t _ What would be the effects of decreasing the effective tax rate, thereby causing the NIT schedule to shift from NIT to NIT ?

The table shows the costs of two milk producers. costs per litre firm X $9 firm Y $7 The price received by producers is $12 per litre. Both firms have been given quotas allowing them to produce 200 litres per day. Assuming constant costs of production and zero costs of entry and exit, what is the maximum price firm Y would be willing to pay (per day) to buy X’s quota?
Which trade-off do governments face when they embark upon the privatisation of a state monopoly?

options.B: between introducing competition and maximising revenue from the privatisation
options.D: between pursuing short-run and long-run profit maximisation

questions.questionText: The graphs show how consumer prices and real GDP changed in a country between 2000 and 2010. consumer prices (% increase on a year earlier) 200001 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 092010 real GDP (% increase on a year earlier) 200001 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 092010 Which conclusion may be drawn from the graphs?

options.A: The level of real GDP was lower in 2010 than in 2005.
options.B: The price level fell between 2005 and 2008.
options.C: Living standards remained roughly constant between 2000 and 2010.
options.D: The country experienced continuous economic growth between 2000 and 2010.

questions.questionText: What will be the short-run effect on the level of output of an increase in the money supply, according to Keynesian theory (assuming the liquidity trap does not apply) and according to monetarist theory (assuming the increase is unanticipated)? effect on output Keynesian theory monetarist theory
What, according to the accelerator principle, will cause the level of investment to fall?

options.B: a decrease in the rate of growth of national income
options.C: an increase in the price of capital equipment
options.D: an increase in the rate of interest

questions.questionText: A developing economy’s exports are price inelastic in demand, while its imports are price elastic. What would cause a rise in GDP and a fall in the deficit on the current account of the balance of payments?

options.B: a fall in the price of its imports
options.C: a reduction in the existing quota limits imposed on its exports
options.D: the development abroad of synthetic substitutes for its exports

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government, the value of the investment multiplier is 4. By how much will consumption increase, if investment increases by $200?

In a banking system, all banks maintain 10% of deposits as cash. Customers withdraw $20000 in cash. Assuming no subsequent net change in notes and coins in circulation, by how much will the banks have to reduce their net loans?
If the money supply is fixed, an increase in economic activity

options.A: increases the transactions demand for money.
options.D: reduces the income velocity of circulation.

questions.questionText: What will be the likely effects on interest rates and bond prices of a decrease in the demand for money? interest rates bond prices

In an economy, the volume of output falls by 2% in a year, while the quantity of money rises by 3%. If the velocity of circulation of money remains the same, what will be the approximate increases in the price level and the money value of national income? increase in money increase in price level value of national income
A country has a high ratio of investment to GDP and rapid economic growth. If the net capital inflow from abroad is zero, what will be a necessary cost of such growth?

options.B: increased consumption of luxury goods by richer residents
options.C: increased imports of goods from abroad
options.D: the sacrifice of present consumption by residents of the country

questions.questionText: Why may an economy experience an increase in potential economic growth despite net investment remaining unchanged?

options.C: The new capital equipment embodies more advanced technology.
options.D: The new capital equipment is longer lasting than the capital equipment it replaces.

questions.questionText: It is often argued that the UN Human Development Index is a better indicator of economic development than income per capita because it adjusts for

options.A: average hours worked by the population.
